claims.text: The initial alloy has a metastable, non-equilibrium microstructure.
The initial microstructure contains a solid-solution matrix and intermetallic compounds.
The initial intermetallic compounds include Mg-rich phases.
The initial intermetallic compounds are fine, small, and homogeneously dispersed.
The lightweight alloy has a density below 6 g/cm3.
The alloy is produced by induction melting under non-equilibrium conditions.
Annealing promotes microstructural evolution toward a more stable structure.
Thermally activated diffusion during annealing coarsens Mg-rich intermetallic compounds.
Annealing causes Mg-rich intermetallic phases to segregate preferentially at grain boundaries.
Coarsening and segregation alter the local surface and near-surface elemental composition.
The altered local chemistry promotes preferential formation of a continuous MgO-containing scale during high-temperature oxidation.
Segregation creates chemically heterogeneous regions that interfere with formation of a uniform passive film during corrosion.
Annealed samples will form thicker high-temperature oxide scales than the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples will form more adherent high-temperature oxide scales than the as-cast baseline.
The more continuous and adherent scale will enhance high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Annealed samples will exhibit higher or more variable corrosion current densities because passivation is disrupted.
The proposed pathway applies when annealing remains below the alloy's incipient melting point.
Large changes in composition or extreme annealing temperatures may produce different transformation pathways.

contradictions.description: The initial state is described as both 'as-cast, homogenized' and as an untreated as-cast, non-equilibrium baseline. Homogenization is itself a heat treatment, so the intended pre-annealing control state is ambiguous.
